page: Amazon Web Services g4dn.xlarge is a GPU-accelerated instance designed for graphics-intensive and machine learning workloads. Powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it features an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor with 4 vCPUs (2 physical cores) running at 2.5 GHz, paired with 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory. The hardware configuration includes a dedicated NVIDIA Turing T4 GPU with 16 GB of VRAM and a local 125 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance tradeoff. Standard CPU-bound operations, memory bandwidth, and general-purpose processing tasks score in the lower tiers, with stress-ng, Geekbench, and Passmark results consistently falling into the bottom 25% or bottom 10% categories. Conversely, the integrated NVIDIA T4 GPU delivers exceptional performance for specialized tasks. LLM inference benchmarks for small (135M) and medium (7B) models achieve top-tier (top 10%) and strong (top 25%) results, processing prompts at up to 8,452.97 tokens per second and generating text at up to 304.07 tokens per second.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the g4dn.xlarge offers an accessible entry point for GPU-accelerated computing without the overhead of larger multi-GPU configurations. The inclusion of local NVMe SSD storage and dedicated GPU resources provides a balanced profile for specific workloads. It is highly suited for small-to-medium LLM inference, graphics-intensive rendering, machine learning model deployment, and applications requiring hardware acceleration combined with local high-speed storage.
